message: Kernel benchmark accepted. Finish B's actual resident trainer lifecycle qualification using retained inputs, without another benchmark setup round. Queue behind existing owned work; do not interrupt active jobs.
implementation: Thin adapter around the resident full trainer, not custom compute loop. Keep normal validation/checkpoint/finalization. Pin effective config and source before launch; record actual data order and optimizer events. Test missing weights/images, output collision, accidental downloads/resume, event accounting and diagnostic validation roles. Existing input integrity and resident-environment checks still apply; no repeated backend smoke before execution.
execution: After scoped adapter tests/preflight pass, register locally and execute two fresh isolated repetitions; return source and evidence together. Expected128batches and8optimizer updates/epoch,16updates/run. A mismatch is a reported failure, not permission to patch trainer internals or relax accounting. First error/OOM stops both; no retry. Broader changes return for review first.
acceptance: Complete lifecycle events, actual update/validation counts, finite losses, setup/train/validation/save/final-validation timings without double counting, peak memory and exact checkpoint hashes. Verify resident checkpoint reload and finite predictions on the same two training smoke examples; no quality gate. Retain weights locally. This qualifies a full trainer path, not Mac speed, kernel speed ratio or held-out accuracy.
return: One named source/report archive: at most100regular files,20MBexpanded,5MBper member. No weights/images/caches. Exact size/hash receipt flow; sender retains originals and owns shared-copy cleanup.
boundaries: No install/download, new corpus/admission, private focus transfer, capture, Git writes, export, promotion, automatic sweep or duplication of local Run027/028. C/D still require their eligible model/evaluation bundle.
next_owner: Big Dog: implement, verify and execute bounded lifecycle. NUIAK: accept evidence and prepare subsequent eligible model workload.
